speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the initial lab results; now, does your dizziness occur in brief, spinning episodes triggered by head movements, or is it a constant sensation unrelated to your position? REQUEST TEST: Complete blood count, Comprehensive metabolic panel, Thyroid-stimulating hormone, Electrocardiogram, Hearing test.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lab results are all normal, which is good. To narrow this down, do you notice any ringing in your ears, hearing loss, or a feeling of fullness in your affected ear during these episodes?

REQUEST TEST: Audiometry, Vestibular function tests
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with internal auditory canals

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Audiometry: Bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, consistent with presbycusis. No sudden drops in hearing indicative of Meniere's disease or labyrinthitis. Vestibular_Function_Tests: Videonystagmography shows normal vestibular response except for response elicited during Dix-Hallpike maneuver, consistent with BPPV. MRI_Brain: No evidence of central lesions or infarcts that would suggest central causes of vertigo.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
